experiment.question: When a decision system chooses between places, does it choose ones that keep the seat out of enemy sight?
experiment.hypothesis: A brain that uses the places' facts (hidden, route exposure) spends a smaller share of the following five seconds in an enemy's sight line than a random chooser offered the same places through the same navigator. If it does not, the choice of place is not what reduces exposure here.

primaryMetric.label: Exposure in the window after
primaryMetric.description: Mean over the selected decisions of the share of window samples in which some enemy held a sight line to the seat.

decisionType.rule: Beneficial: in the window the seat did not die, took no damage, and was in some enemy's sight line in at most 25% of exposure samples (at most a quarter of the time seen). Harmful: it died, or took at least 25 damage (a quarter of full health). Otherwise neutral.
decisionType.applies: An executed decision whose go choice is PLACE_n, taken when at least two places were offered, and which bound a place.

definition.question: When a decision system chooses between places, does it choose ones that keep the seat out of enemy sight?
definition.hypothesis: A brain that uses the places' facts (hidden, route exposure) spends a smaller share of the following five seconds in an enemy's sight line than a random chooser offered the same places through the same navigator. If it does not, the choice of place is not what reduces exposure here.
definition.notes: The navigator walks wherever it is told and never chooses; the place is the brain's. Arms with brain jev or llm call paid APIs and run only with JEV_LIVE_TEST=1 / LLM_LIVE_TEST=1; without the flag they are recorded as PENDING and nothing is filled in for them.

skirmisher chose move=HOLD in 100.0% of 1525 decisions where the move axis offered a choice (threshold 95%).
possibleCauses: a policy that does one thing (true of scripted policies)
the other options are never worth choosing in this environment

warnings.message: skirmisher chose target=TARGET_0 in 98.9% of 186 decisions where the target axis offered a choice (threshold 95%).
possibleCauses: a policy that does one thing (true of scripted policies)
the other options are never worth choosing in this environment

warnings.message: skirmisher chose slot 0 of the target axis in 95.7% of 46 decisions with two or more slots offered; a position-blind chooser would pick it 46.4% of the time.
possibleCauses: model preference for what slot 0 is (nearest cover, nearest enemy)
option-order bias: preference for the first option shown
an environment where the first-listed option really is best
controller dominance: the choice matters little either way

warnings.message: On exposure_fraction_next_window, skirmisher is not distinguishable from random (random choices through the same controllers): paired difference -0.096 with a 95% interval [-0.794, 0.602] over 3 seeds.
possibleCauses: the deterministic controller solves most of the task
the metric does not depend on the choices the brain makes
too few seeds to separate them

notes: Episodes are the unit of every interval. Episodes on the same seed start the same match but diverge: frame pacing is not deterministic.
Decision-level pools overlap in time; their n overstates independent evidence.
